name: NewsletterPlatform.com – Newsletters & Email Marketing
author: Plugins.shop

sections.description:
Create WordPress newsletters, manage subscribers and automate welcome emails with your configured mail provider. No developer account, licence key or WooCommerce required.

Free demo | Pro demo | Documentation

Hosted demos disable sending/live automation and expire in 30 minutes. Use fictional data. Demo versions/privacy.

Included in Free

  • Newsletter editor: ten editable designs, reusable blocks, previews, autosave, undo and revisions.
  • Subscriber management: tags, reviewed CSV imports/exports and consent records.
  • Signup forms: block/shortcode placement, unchecked consent and double opt-in.
  • Welcome automation: multi-email sequences with delays and optional WooCommerce coupons.
  • Campaigns: sender setup, tests, audience review, scheduling and queue recovery.
  • Preferences: topics, frequency limits, pauses, unsubscribe and suppression.
  • Roles and reports: newsletter roles, optional click reports and signed SendGrid feedback.

Optional Pro companion

Separate paid Pro adds 72 designs, kits, conditional journeys, saved audiences, publisher workflows, A/B tests, digests, approvals and enhanced reports. Free has eight static Pro examples. Pro removal retains content and holds dependent work.

Related Plugins.shop tools

No automatic integration:

  • KillerConversions – Reader enquiry forms.
  • ClickClue – Eligible visit recordings with privacy controls.
  • CampaignBars – Announcements linking to a signup page or offer.

Source: source-code.txt. Limits: usage-notes.txt. History: changelog.txt.

Privacy and stored data

The site database stores subscribers, consent, preferences, drafts and delivery metadata. Signup records contain name/email, consent wording/timestamps, source/locale, a bounded browser user-agent and keyed network-address hash. Expiring rate limits prevent abuse. No contacts or usage telemetry go to the developer; mail providers process delivery.

Confirmation/unsubscribe links require explicit submission. Providers have a separate RFC 8058 one-click POST endpoint.

WordPress privacy export/erasure is supported. Erasure retains a keyed suppression marker against accidental reimport/resubscription.

The optional admin review invitation stores save dates and account/site preferences locally. Overview shows it after 30 days and activity on three separate days, with 30-day snooze/permanent dismissal. No review records go to the developer. Clicking contacts WordPress.org but does not confirm review submission.

Click measurement starts off and needs administrator acknowledgement, which is not subscriber consent. Contacts can be excluded. Requests may include scanners/forwarded messages, not verified human engagement. Reports add no open pixels, tracking cookies, IP-address records or user-agent histories. Hosting/provider logs and signup consent records are separate.

Form dismissal uses browser-tab session storage; signup completion uses a functional cookie. Private CSV jobs expire after 24 hours on scheduled cleanup; completion/cancellation clears raw CSV. Personal reporting retention is 30-365 days; operational log retention is configurable. Scheduled cleanup removes sent/cancelled/skipped queue records and attempts after 90 days, retaining receipts for unresolved campaigns. Failed/unknown work stays for review. SendGrid correlation/events have 90-day scheduled retention. Consent/suppression remain separately; provider suppression fingerprints remain until explicit plugin-data deletion.

Uninstall keeps data unless Delete on uninstall is enabled. WooCommerce coupons remain merchant records. Preserve Free, link mappings and signing material so issued links work. Read usage-notes.txt for legacy-link and migration limits.

External services

WordPress mail transport

Tests/campaigns/automations/confirmations pass recipients, content and headers to wp_mail() and your configured mail service. Configure it separately and review its terms/privacy policy. Transport acceptance is not proof of inbox delivery.

Optional SendGrid feedback

Requires a SendGrid account, configured SMTP, HTTPS webhook and public verification key. Messages include an opaque correlation value. Signed SendGrid events are verified locally; correlated hard bounces/complaints suppress delivery. No SendGrid API calls or SMTP configuration.

SendGrid | Twilio terms | Privacy policy

Optional public-link checks and URL validation

Requested checks send HEAD without redirects to eligible public links/images in a saved draft. Destinations receive the URL, server IP and checker user-agent, not recipients, cookies or credentials. Action/account/personalized/tracking URLs are excluded. Supported cURL/public IPv4 is required; unchecked links are not verified.

Privacy-URL validation, including campaign preparation, and requested link checks resolve hostnames through the server DNS resolver. It receives the hostname; this is DNS validation, not vendor API/telemetry.

Remote images, links and local workspace requests

Inserted remote images can load in editing previews and email clients; their hosts may receive device IP and browser/client request information. Links contact their destination when opened. Use trusted destinations and review their policies.

Workspace API requests go to this site’s REST endpoints. Bundled designs, example images and More Plugins assets are local. The catalog does not fetch remote data, track views or install plugins. Product, publisher, author and documentation links open only when clicked. Free has no vendor telemetry, account requirement, licensing request, remote template service or private updater.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate Free. Network-wide activation is unsupported.
  2. Complete sender setup: identity, owned test inbox, mailing address and privacy URL. Partial setup saves.
  3. Configure mail transport separately; save a draft and inspect a test in your inbox.
  4. Confirm the production site, turn off test mode and enable campaigns/forms separately.
  5. Import permission-based contacts; active imports need consent provenance. Imports send no confirmations/welcomes.
  6. Add the signup block or [newsletterplatform_com_signup]. Review audience/holds before scheduling.

Sending/forms start disabled; saving settings enables neither. Enabled forms can send confirmations while campaigns pause. Changed URLs/non-production sites hold mail; identical clones cannot be detected. Only first individual activation redirects. Old shortcodes work.
sections.faq:
Is Free a trial?

No trial expiry or paid subscriber cap. Free sends real newsletters; administrators control test mode. Operational limits still apply.

Do I need SMTP?

Configure WordPress mail separately; SMTP is one option. Sending uses wp_mail(). Host/provider and operational limits apply regardless of payment; see usage-notes.txt.

Can Free automate several welcome emails?

Yes: one active signup welcome, up to 50 messages with delays. New eligible confirmations enroll; imports/updates do not enroll old contacts. Subscriber preferences still apply.

Is WooCommerce required?

Only for product blocks, checkout consent and coupons. Classic checkout needs WooCommerce 8.0; Checkout Block consent needs its additional fields API. Purchases never subscribe customers.

How do I migrate an older installation?

Back up first. Current newsletterplatform-com installations: replace Free then matching Pro, without uninstalling.

Old newsletter-platform: update to 1.0.8, deactivate old Free/Pro, activate renamed Free and complete Plugins > Newsletter data upgrade before Pro. Never uninstall/reactivate old copies. Existing multisite needs coordinated migration; automatic migration is refused.

pluginsshop-newsletter-platform 1.0.9 shares storage: deactivate both old copies without uninstalling, let jobs finish, then activate new Free/Pro. Preserve old image URLs. Read usage-notes.txt before migrating.
sections.changelog:
1.0.10

  • First WordPress.org release; earlier versions were not directory releases.
  • Add an optional honest-review invitation with 30-day snooze and permanent dismissal.
  • Share the footer review link and local preferences across Free/Pro; sending is unchanged.
